newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index jumps to new highs in morning.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index jumps to new highs in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped 166 points to an all time high of 14,923, chiefly due to renewed interest in 'pink' utility shares, brokers said.
The index advanced further to 14,929, a gain of 171 points, on very heavy turnover of HK$2.73 billion in the first 15 minutes of trade.
Pink chips are blue chip companies with China earnings potential.
"Hongkong Telecom accounts for a good portion of that (gain in the index)," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.
The telecommunications giant advanced to a new 1997 high of HK$17.95, then eased to trade HK$0.50 higher at HK$17.65 on robust turnover of HK$224 million.
China Light and Power rose to a year high of HK$40.40, a gain of HK$1.60 on trade of HK$213 million.
Indosuez W.I. Carr director of Asian utilities research Alice Hui said she has a target price of HK$44.50 for the share for 1997.
Brokers said the market was showing a continuation of last week's strength, a follow-through of the rally on Wall Street and at home, brokers said.
"We could trade in a wide range, 100 points plus or minus, but I think we will finish on the plus side," said Alistair Candlish, head of derivatives trading at Indosuez W.I. Carr.
The Hang Seng Index gained 341 points to close at an all time high of 14,757.81, and the Dow Industrials rose 0.86 of a point to 7,331.04 on Friday.
The commercial and industrial sector was also strong on Monday morning. Swire Pacific A put on HK$1.50 to HK$66.50 and Wharf added HK$0.90 to HK$35.60.
Red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises was trading HK$4.00 higher at HK$49.20, after hitting a high of HK$49.60.
